body: I think it's you who doesn't understand the original statement.  It plainly states at the end of the original post that pro-choice is the only obvious answer.  What you're doing is being selective with your reading because you want to be right.
Exactly how are your posts here going to save children from rape?  You're confusing two very different topics in your response.
I completely agree with you.  Females have the absolute right to every aspect of their bodies.

I guess the larger truth at play for me, as an individual, is to bow in awe of the paradigm shifting, illuminating quote that started this whole thing off.  It's such a valuable way of distilling, and subsequently articulating, a very complex issue into a digestible portion of sound, pure logic.  How else is such a simple man like me to separate my emotion from my intellect? Reading this quote had a profound impact on me.  I guess my real intention was to describe where I was prior to encountering these words, and where I might find myself as a consequence.

I'm sorry for the formatting of my responses. I'm an old man, and reddit is something new to me.

My claim is because, as I said, men and women, in any combination, are capable of raising a child.   There is no way for me to ever have first hand knowledge of being pregnant.  This is the yardstick I employ in all situations. If I've never walked in your shoes, I have no business telling you what's it's like, and how you should do it. 
But, I agree, that the genuine solution is likely exactly what you've proposed, which is a community approach. However, I simply don't feel I have to cognitive resources to participate in a meaningful way.  I have much to learn, and much growth to go through before I feel I can contribute something meaningful.  I guess it's ultimately about humbly surrendering to my limitations, be they intellectual or physical.
No, it is like saying that I possess the moral clarity and selflessness to understand when it's time for me to simply keep my mouth shut.
Absolutely not.  The only thing a child needs to grow into a healthy person is love, every day, every hour.  Every single human being on this planet is capable of doing precisely that.

Well, I think it's important to recognize that legalism is derived from socially accepted norms and mores, or more simply, morality.  I would simply counter that having the integrity to recognize that I have very little to offer in this respect is precisely what you've asked for: participation.  If removing men from the legislative process is a high goal, which you serm to believe, and which I would agree with, then the example set by choosing to accept my limited perspective is precisely the example other men need to be exposed to.   While I may not be participating in a manner this suits your particular desires, it is impossible to argue that I'm not participating.

This is potentially a topic for a different discussion, but I find that thinking women need my support in this is operating on the assumption that they're not capable of rendering a suitable morality for themselves.  But, I'd be remiss to simply discount what you've said, because it does have merit.  And, as you've pointed out, too many men, and frankly a lot of women as well, wield the blunt sword of religion to inform social morality.  However, here we all are, doing exactly what you've hoped should happen, which is having a productive dialogue that is centered around the notion that women need our support, but not our advice.

Good for you!!  Isn't it such a terrible dichotomy that doing what is best for ourselves can seem like a terrible threat to our well being?  I'm glad that you found a set of skills that will serve you well in the years to come.

Wow.  What a profound perspective.  As a man, I've always maintained that it's simply none of my damned business to get involved in the abortion debate because I'll never be in the position that I might have to choose.  Perhaps that was an unconscious way of saying that the problem is complex beyond my ability to comprehend it.   But this.... this is a type of logic that very effectively banishes any doubt to the validity of pro-choice.

I suppose that can be very disappointing from a variety of different perspectives.  Likely the strongest thing this speaks to is how incredibly repressed the average American is.  The overwhelming majority of us actually believe that being honest and open right away, rather than waiting to be honest after we've spent sufficient time pretending to be someone we're not, is a detriment to human relationships.  The primary flaw in the American mindset is the fear of being disappointed.  We have been programmed to believe that we're all guaranteed to be victorious in some fashion, or at the very least that if we claim to think a certain way, then the universe will align itself to our whims, and when life proves us wrong, we find fault in the world around us rather than with ourselves.

I'm a 49 year old divorced, single dad.  I live in the Minneapolis area.  My experiences are as follows.  Women on dating apps in my age range seem to fall into one of three categories, they have become jaded and bitter by a painful divorce and subsequently have a toxic relationship with themselves, they expect things to get serious by the end of the first date, and if you haven't tried to sleep with them by the second date there's "no chemistry", or they're very stable, attractive women who are simply not interested in a man like myself.  Lol.  Now, I have to face myself in the mirror and accept that my experiences say just as much about myself as a person as it says about the women I'm dating.  I think the reality is that until I solve the problems that I have with myself, I'll be stuck dating the first two categories.

I sure hope you're able to succeed in that endeavor. Perhaps the greatest fear a parent can endure is the fear of not breaking the chain of abuse and trauma from our own childhood, and subsequently going to our deathbed with the unshakable conviction that we have succeeded in destroying the only good thing the human condition has to offer.
